fact_sheet.business_description: Apple sells consumer devices integrated with proprietary software and services [D01]. The iPhone is the central product, supported by a broad installed base, applications, accessories and customer accounts [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Consumer devices (iPhone) and integrated services [D01]. Customers benefit from ecosystem convenience, which can produce repeat purchases and switching costs [D01].
economics: Operating margins were 31.2% (2011), 35.3% (2012), 28.7% (2013), 28.7% (2014) and 30.5% (2015) [D02]. Return on equity (proxy) ranged from 30.0% to 44.7% over the same period [D02]. Economics are determined by customer retention, replacement frequency, pricing and the required cost of innovation [D01].
earnings_record: Revenue grew from $108.2bn (2011) to $233.7bn (2015) [D02]. Net income grew from $25.9bn (2011) to $53.4bn (2015) [D02]. Recent performance shows cyclical contraction; Q2 FY2016 revenue fell 12.8% and EPS fell 18.5% year-over-year [D03].
competitive_position: The company is a premium consumer franchise [D05]. Competitors include Samsung and other Android-based phones [D06]. Moat evidence relies on ecosystem convenience, though it remains exposed to technology, premium pricing, and concentrated hardware demand [D01].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: As of 2016-03-26, cash and marketable securities were $232.9bn against $79.9bn in debt (including commercial paper) [D04]. Net cash position is $153.1bn [D04].
management_and_capital_allocation: The capital-return program is expanded to $250 billion, with $163 billion returned to shareholders through March 2016 [D03]. Management's record includes significant buybacks, though authorization is not execution [D01, D03].

yields_pct.basis: FY2015 FCF yield provided in [D04]; trailing earnings yield derived from reciprocal of P/E [D04]; US Treasury 10-year yield from [D04].

what_the_market_is_worried_about: Dependence on a single upgrade cycle [D05].
Impact of China demand, foreign exchange, and carrier behavior [D05].
recent_events: Q2 FY2016 earnings report published 2016-04-26, showing revenue contraction [D03].
berkshire_context: Berkshire cash $61.2bn as of year-end 2015 [D08]. Investment deputies have discretion over smaller portfolios [D08]. No current-quarter holdings disclosed [D08].

understandable.evidence: Apple functions as a consumer franchise with significant brand loyalty and ecosystem switching costs, which provide a degree of predictability despite the tech industry's speed [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: The company maintains a premium consumer franchise supported by ecosystem convenience, which encourages repeat purchases and creates switching costs for customers [D01], [D05].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: Revenue and net income have grown significantly from 2011 to 2015 [D02], and while recent results show cyclical contraction, the core franchise remains robust [D03].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The company maintains a very strong balance sheet with a net cash position of $153.1 billion [D04] and has demonstrated high returns on equity ranging from 30.0% to 44.7% [D02].

capital_intensity.evidence: The business generates high free cash flow relative to its capital requirements, evidenced by an FCF yield of 13.63% [D04].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Management has demonstrated an owner-oriented approach by returning $163 billion to shareholders through an expanded capital-return program [D03].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: With a market capitalization of approximately $513.55 billion, this investment is of sufficient scale to be meaningful for Berkshire [D04].

price_screen.evidence: The FCF yield of 13.63% significantly exceeds the ~3% threshold (1.5x the 1.83% long bond yield) [D04].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a powerful consumer franchise with immense cash generation, a fortress balance sheet, and high returns on capital

gate2.why_available: The market is currently fixated on a cyclical revenue contraction and fears regarding smartphone saturation [D03], [D05]. We disagree, viewing the business as a durable consumer franchise whose ecosystem lock-in will endure despite short-term hardware volatility [D01]. The discount provided by Mr. Market allows us to acquire this cash-generative power at a low P/E of 10.39x [D04].
evidence: Market concerns focus on smartphone saturation and reliance on upgrade cycles [D05].
Q2 FY2016 results show a temporary revenue decline of 12.8% [D03].
Company maintains a fortress balance sheet with $153.1 billion in net cash [D04].
FCF yield of 13.63% indicates an attractive valuation relative to historical earnings power [D04].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market views Apple's recent revenue contraction as evidence of a structural decline in its growth prospects rather than a temporary cyclical adjustment [D03], [D05].
what_must_be_true: The core ecosystem benefits (switching costs, brand loyalty) remain intact
The smartphone market has not reached a point of permanent, value-destroying commoditization
Management continues to prioritize shareholder returns through disciplined capital allocation

gate3.owner_earnings_per_share: Not provided; using FY2015 FCF yield of 13.63% [D04] as proxy for owner earnings.

key_assumptions: Smartphone market is not permanently commoditized [D01]

gate3.price_vs_value: Price (10.39x P/E) is below conservative low-end valuation; provides margin of safety.
gate3.alternatives: Existing holdings or Berkshire buybacks; current Apple valuation offers a superior earnings yield vs low bond rates [D04].
gate3.downside_case: Permanent loss unlikely due to $153.1bn net cash position [D04]; downside involves multiple contraction if ecosystem fails.
flagged_assumptions: FY2015 FCF yield is treated as a reasonable proxy for normalized owner earnings in the absence of explicit owner-earnings calculations in pack [D04].

gate4.role_description: permanent_passive_holder — value realised by the business compounding and rational capital allocation; Berkshire's edge is patience and permanent capital [D08].
value_realisation_path: Compounding of intrinsic value through ecosystem-driven earnings growth and disciplined capital return programs [D01], [D03].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: Post-1980, we treat significant equity investments as permanent holdings in wonderful consumer franchises, relying on the business's internal compounding rather than active control or restructuring [D01].

kill_criteria: Ecosystem convenience and switching costs erode due to successful platform-agnostic service competition [D01].
Smartphone market experiences permanent, value-destroying commoditization where Apple loses premium pricing power [D05].
Capital allocation becomes undisciplined or management abandons the owner-oriented approach [D03].
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Must maintain cash floor of at least $30B [D08]. Investment must avoid triggering regulatory ownership thresholds without permission [D08].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Higher than current equity holdings or Berkshire share repurchases given the 13.63% FCF yield relative to a 1.83% long bond yield [D04].
gate5.decider_reason: The investment represents a significant allocation into a powerful consumer franchise that meets our criteria for a permanent holding, fitting the scale and nature of my direct oversight.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: A structural loss of pricing power due to permanent commoditization of the smartphone industry would undermine the core economic thesis of the ecosystem.

valuation.owner_earnings: FY2015 FCF of $53.4B used as a proxy [D04]
valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction if ecosystem loyalty erodes, mitigated by $153.1B net cash [D04]

drivers.driver: The company trades at a P/E of 10.39x and an FCF yield of 13.63%, which compares favorably to the 1.83% long-term bond yield [D04].
Apple possesses a durable consumer franchise with high switching costs and brand loyalty that sustains long-term pricing power [D01, D05].
The company maintains an exceptional balance sheet with $153.1 billion in net cash, providing a substantial margin of safety [D04].
Management has demonstrated an owner-oriented focus by returning $163 billion to shareholders through disciplined capital allocation [D03].
The market's fixation on temporary cyclical smartphone contraction ignores the underlying strength of the persistent ecosystem [D03, D05].

kill_criteria: Ecosystem convenience and switching costs erode due to successful platform-agnostic service competition [D01].
Smartphone market experiences permanent, value-destroying commoditization where Apple loses premium pricing power [D05].
Capital allocation becomes undisciplined or management abandons the owner-oriented approach [D03].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the smartphone ecosystem is commoditizing, resulting in a permanent loss of pricing power and customer loyalty.
final.memo:
Apple sells consumer devices integrated with proprietary software and services, creating an ecosystem that consumers value for its convenience [D01]. We understand this business because it functions as a powerful consumer franchise, where the loyalty of the installed base creates significant switching costs [D01].

The economics of the business are characterized by consistently high returns on equity, which have ranged from 30.0% to 44.7% between 2011 and 2015 [D02]. Apple generates massive free cash flow, and its strong competitive position is supported by its ability to maintain premium pricing in a competitive market [D01, D04].

Management has proven themselves to be able and owner-minded, having returned $163 billion to shareholders through an expanded capital-return program as of March 2016 [D03]. This disciplined approach to capital allocation demonstrates a clear commitment to maximizing long-term shareholder value [D03].

Mr. Market is currently preoccupied with cyclical revenue contraction and fears of smartphone saturation, leading to a valuation that we find attractive [D03, D05]. We believe the market is misjudging the durability of Apple's ecosystem, allowing us to acquire a wonderful business at a fair price [D01, D04].

With an FCF yield of 13.63% against a long bond yield of 1.83%, the initial earnings yield is highly compelling [D04]. We view the intrinsic value as significantly higher than the current price, providing a solid margin of safety [D04].

Our primary risk is a structural decline in pricing power should the smartphone market become permanently commoditized [D05]. We will hold this position as long as the ecosystem remains intact and management continues to act in the interest of owners [D03, D05].
